verdict.rationale: Bevy's primary language is Rust itself. All engine and game logic runs through Bevy ECS, with components as plain Rust structs and systems as normal Rust functions, so the language exposes the engine API natively. Productivity is backed by the 'fast compiles' claim and community praise for ergonomics, though one user doubts that a dogmatic ECS approach is more productive. Missing for 10: any evidence of a debugger or debugging workflow, independent confirmation of iteration-speed productivity, and evidence that the full API surface is documented beyond the reference docs.

support.subject: As a game developer, the primary scripting language is productive and fully exposes the engine API, with a debugger behind it

citations.quote: All engine and game logic uses Bevy ECS, a custom Entity Component System
Components: Rust structs that implement the Component trait
With Bevy you can expect 0.8-3.0 seconds with the "fast compiles" configuration
this is by far the most thought out, ergonomic and complete thing I found
